subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls to `openclaw cron add` and `openclaw cron edit`, or should the current global `cron.retry` policy remain the supported surface?
rationale: The runtime recovery problem is partially solved globally, but per-job retry count/delay/backoff controls would become a new public cron API and stored job contract.

options.title: Add Per-Job Retry Policy
options.body: Add stored job-level retry settings, wire them through cron add/edit/show/list/docs, and let global `cron.retry` remain the default when a job does not override it.

options.title: Keep Global Retry Only
options.body: Keep `cron.retry.maxAttempts` and `cron.retry.backoffMs` as the supported surface and close or narrow this issue to documentation/status wording.

options.title: Fold Into Guardrails Work
options.body: Defer per-job controls and make the broader reason-aware cron guardrail issue own retry policy, retry reasons, and circuit-breaker semantics together.

recommendation.title: Add Per-Job Retry Policy
recommendation.body: Add stored job-level retry settings, wire them through cron add/edit/show/list/docs, and let global `cron.retry` remain the default when a job does not override it.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent global recurring retry implementation and area history make this the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
